author: sjm41
body:
* **InterPro ID / label**
Methylcytosine dioxygenase TET1/2/3 IPR040175

* **Example sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Fly 'Tet' gene (FBgn0263392/M9NEY8)

* **Description of issue**
Current InterPro2GO annotations are:
[chromosomal 5-methylcytosine DNA demethylation, oxidation pathway (GO:0141167)](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/GTerm?id=GO:0141167)
Molecular Function
[5-methylcytosine dioxygenase activity (GO:0070579)](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/GTerm?id=GO:0070579)

But unlike mammalian TET, the fly ortholog catalyses demethylation of methyl**adenosine** in DNA.
I.e fly Tet has EC:1.14.11.51 = GO:0141131 DNA N6-methyladenine demethylase activity, and not EC:1.14.11.80 = 5-methylcytosine dioxygenase activity (GO:0070579).

So I think the current GO annotations on IPR040175 need moving up the hierarchy a bit.
title: Methylcytosine dioxygenase TET1/2/3 IPR040175

author: blazaropinto
body:
Hi Steven,

Thank you for your message.
I'm confused about this, UniProt says the fly member M9NEY8 is "also able to catalyze the conversion of the modified genomic base 5-methylcytosine (5mC) into 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) (PMID:25936838).", and Rhea gives it EC:1.14.11.80 based on the same paper, is that the protein you were referring to?
Thanks,
Beatriz

author: sjm41
body:
Hi Beatriz

Looking again at the paper (PMID:25936838), the authors say:
- In Drosophila, 5mC modification exists at an extremely low level [Lyko and Maleszka, 2011]
- 5hmC was detected in Drosophila DNA at extremely low levels and fewer than 100 of the cytosine bases per genome were modified to be 5hmC (this study)
- we first performed an in vitro enzymatic assay and found that the catalytic domain of DMAD (DMAD-CD), but not DMAD-CDmut, could convert 5mC to 5hmC in vitro ([Figures S2]. However, the in vitro activity of DMAD-CD that mediates oxidation of 5mC was about 30-fold lower than that of mouse Tet1-CD.
- Of note, we found no difference in the abundance of 5mC and 5hmC between the wild-type and DMAD mutant flies [Figures 3, S3A, and S3B], strongly arguing that the Drosophila DMAD has no apparent in vivo role in regulating the conversion of 5mC to 5hmC.
- These results together suggest that the DMAD specifically suppresses the in vivo modification of 6mA, rather than 5mC and other methylated DNA bases tested in this study, and m6A in RNA.


So... DMAD (aka Tet/M9NEY8) does show low level EC:1.14.11.80 activity in vitro, but in vivo the main/only activity is EC:1.14.11.51 = GO:0141131.

Therefore, for IPR040175 annotation, I still think that it would be best to use higher level GO terms.
In the related PAINT ticket (#5678), the MF was changed to GO:0016706 2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase activity
I'm not sure how best to replace the current BP term - maybe just remove?

author: blazaropinto
body:
Thank you for looking further into this Steven. I changed [GO:0070579](http://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGo/GTerm?id=GO:0070579) to the parent [GO:0016706](http://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGo/GTerm?id=GO:0016706). As BP term, I updated to the more general [GO:0040029](http://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGo/GTerm?id=GO:0040029). I hope that looks better. The changes will be available in the next InterPro release.
Best,
Beatriz

author: sjm41
body: Thanks Beatriz, looks good to me!
